To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the prediction of lip response to treatment using the ratio of the mean of soft to hard tissue changes is less accurate than the prediction of lip movement using a stepwise multiple regression model.
the use of multiple regression analysis to predict lip movement is a slightly more accurate method than the ratio of the mean prediction and that the accuracy of prediction is still low.
the prediction of soft-tissue response to orthodontics is a complex issue and that a combination of different methods is necessary to achieve an optimal outcome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction of lip response to the orthodontic treatment.
the development of a more precise estimation method for the prediction of soft tissues changes related to the tooth movements than simple relationships between hard and soft tissues.
the accuracy of prediction equations in orthodontics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multiple regression model appears to be useful and accurate in predicting soft tissue changes in the upper and lower lips in the extraction group and in the non-extraction group.
the multiple regression technique appears to be slightly more accurate than ratio prediction (Viewbox 5.0 software) in predicting the lip response to orthodntic treatment.
the use of a regression model is a more precise method than simple ratio of means in prediction of soft tissue response to orthodontics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prediction of lip movement using a multivarable regression analysis is slightly more accurate than a simple ratio of the means.
the prediction of the soft tissue response to orthodontics is a complex process that is influenced by several variables, and the use of multiple regression analysis is a promising approach.
multiple regression analysis can be a useful tool to predict lip movements during treatment, but its accuracy is still not high enough for routine clinical application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a multivariable approach to predicting lip changes may be more accurate than a simple ratio approach.
the accuracy of the prediction of soft-tissue changes can be improved using a multivarable model.

the prediction of the soft tissue response is not an exact science and the clinician should be prepared to accept the fact that the actual soft tissue changes will be different from the predicted changes.
